reverse_outline.summary: Chapter preview: five T&S functions, shared vs local parts, and propagating one enforcement decision
Business stakes: trust drives liquidity, and the DSA makes decisions regulator-auditable
Architectural stakes: T&S spans every context, so it needs one decision record and propagation path
Three key points: separate functions joined by one record, enforcement done only when propagated, measure harm not activity
Failure patterns addressed: moderation as afterthought, ghost inventory, set-and-forget AI
T&S grows piecemeal into incompatible stacks that cannot say what was removed and whether it disappeared
Chapter thesis: T&S as a platform capability of separate functions, full propagation, harm metrics, shared machinery with local policy
Roadmap of the chapter's sections and evidence sources
Scope boundaries: fraud, identity and regulation belong to other chapters; Veldmark is the running example

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 60 aligned units' reverse-outline summaries state the controlling idea of the spec paragraph they align to, in spec order; the five callouts match no spec paragraph and are expected.

Only Architecture ¶8 was flagged two_ideas. Its two cases (Which? edits, leboncoin) sit under one lead sentence, 'Two public cases show why the mode matters', and the spec's p23 declares exactly that two-lesson controlling idea, so the unit holds one controlling idea with two supports.
Every unit supports one of S1-S6 or the scene/intro/conclusion framing; the Keybridge paragraph (p50) and failure mode 10 are spec-declared.

Each table is introduced and followed by its reading (inventory -> totals; functions; policy record -> three consequences; components; modes -> risk tiers; ladder -> fifth column; consumers -> event pattern; notice fields; metrics -> two practices; targets -> p46; share table -> constraint; verticals; trade-offs; decisions). Figures carry explanatory captions and are referred to in text; quotations and statistics (Adevinta, Which?, Transparency Database 4.4 billion / 41%) are interpreted. The unexplained '9 counterparties' and the headcount drop are recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.quote: The failure mode is **Ghost Inventory** caused by enforcement.
results.finding: Declared contrast: 'The event pattern' -> 'What happens without it' (controlling idea: 'Without propagation, enforcement causes Ghost Inventory'). The sentence drops 'without propagation' and attributes Ghost Inventory to enforcement itself, so the contrast with the event pattern is not expressed and the cause is misstated; flow reader A (A3) noticed the same wording.

results.quote: 1. **Moderation only at creation.** Edits, price changes and new photos are not re-scored
results.finding: Declared a contrast sentence at the start of the section ('How to choose well among the alternatives' -> 'How trust and safety goes wrong'). The section opens directly with item 1 of the list; no prose picks up the trade-offs or states the contrast, and the controlling idea's 'each break one part of the design' is also never said.

results.quote: 1. Which component writes moderation decisions, and how many other services restrict content without going through it?
results.finding: Declared a sequence sentence at the start of the section ('The decisions and indicators' -> 'Questions that check them in a review'). The section opens directly with question 1; only the heading carries the boundary, and nothing ties the questions to the Chief Architect's decisions and indicators.

All other declared boundaries (intro p02-p04, the scene, concepts, architecture, enforcement, intake, measuring, sharing, verticals, trade-offs phrase in the options table, CA view, conclusion and its paragraphs) are expressed at the start of the unit as declared.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: The Five Functions of Trust and Safety ¶4
results.quote: The functions also separate the **listing view** from the **actor view**.
results.finding: Both flow readers could not see how this paragraph connects to the five functions and terms around it and read it as an aside ending on a bounded-contexts note. The spec's order (functions, terms, actor view, policy) is fine; the opening verb 'separate' obscures the declared elaboration (decisions about items -> decisions about actors, linked by the decision record).

results.draft_locus: Architecture: The Moderation Pipeline and Its Components ¶2
results.quote: The table is a reference design, so the public record behind it matters.
results.finding: Both readers independently reported that the 'In practice: what is publicly documented' subsection interrupts the walk from the component table into the subsections that explain the components, and both proposed moving it after 'LLMs in the pipeline' (or folding its bullets into the subsections). Both still understood why it is there ('It is in place, but it interrupts'; 'It is not confusing'). The placement is the spec's own decision (flow rationale: public evidence 'right after the component table'), so the difficulty comes from the order, not the prose.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item B4 (A5 here)

results.quote: Femke's bike was marked sold at 18:10 on Monday 8 March and removed from search at 18:11, yet the next morning's alert digest, assembled at 17:30 from an earlier snapshot, still featured it.
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read the timeline: a 'next morning' digest 'assembled at 17:30' reads as after the 18:10 sale until the reader infers 17:30 on Monday. The prose obscures the point (a digest built before the sale shipped after it).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item B5 (A3 here)

results.quote: Figure 4's step that warns the **9 counterparties**, the sellers the account had already reached, is the target design, not what happened in March 2027.
results.finding: Both readers stopped at '9 counterparties': the number appears for the first time (only in the figure), and the scene gave '37 similar messages' withheld from other sellers, with no statement of how many sellers the account had already contacted. The relation between the 9 reached and the 37 withheld is never made.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item B6 (A2 here)

results.quote: The design did not aim to remove moderators; the review headcount follows the review volume.
results.finding: Both readers read this as contradicting the table just above (Tradeyard moderators 158 -> about 135) and had to reconcile it themselves: the text names the 15 moved to sampling and appeals but never says that the remaining drop of about 23 follows from review volume falling from about 138,000 to 96,000.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item B7 (A4 here)

results.quote: 10. **Badges that outlive the account's integrity.** A verified badge stays on an account after it is taken over, and makes the takeover more effective.
results.finding: Both readers found failure mode 10 out of place: unlike items 1-9 it recaps nothing the chapter built (verified badges and account takeover are not discussed in the body). The item is mandated by the spec's p54 controlling idea, and no spec paragraph develops badges or takeover, so the gap is in the spec (either drop the item or give it a basis in the body).
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item B10 (A10 here)

Every does_not_know term is given at or before first substantive use: policy as a versioned record, moderation pipeline, enforcement action, case (Concepts terms); pre- and post-moderation (Moderation modes); prevalence and overturn rate (random sample paragraph, metrics table); trusted flagger (glossed at first use, defined in Notice and action); DSA Arts. 16, 17, 20, 21, 22, 24(5) each explained. Names flow reader B found unintroduced (Common Ground, the architecture advice forum, Keybridge) are on already_knows.
Opens on a concrete history (keyword filter, review queue, report button) and a pointed question; no dictionary definition, sweeping generalisation or announcement.
No 'in conclusion' restatement or new unrelated claim; the closing answers the opening question, replays the incident and hands off.

Synthesis: 'The platform answers it from one record' (what/why/where/how much harm); so-what: 'Such a group answers a regulator, a wrongly blocked seller and its board from the same data; a group of queues answers each with a new project.'

Returns to 'what did we remove last month, why, and did it actually disappear?' and replays 7 March 2027 on the shared platform (POL-FRAUD-PAYLINK, one runtime, sellers warned, hashed phone on Motorvane's block list).

The opening-only reader predicted, in order, the incident and four stacks, the five functions and policies as data, the pipeline (components with public evidence, two speeds, modes, human review, LLMs), enforcement propagation, intake/cases/appeals/statements of reasons, metrics, sharing and verticals, then trade-offs, failure modes, CA view and questions; evidence: DSA, Meta, Stripe, OLX, Adevinta, two dated public cases and fictional Veldmark. This matches every roadmap promise; the opening names the cases only as 'two dated public cases', so the reader could not name Which? and leboncoin, which the opening does not claim to do.

The answer gives EnforcementApplied from the decision service, idempotent apply and acknowledgement, alerts dropping queued notifications and excluding the listing from digests, recommendation eviction, payment hold/freeze per policy, a propagation monitor to the last acknowledgement with 'enforced' separate from 'decided', and demotion as an Article 17 restriction routed through the decision service with a decision record and statement of reasons.

The answer rejects both rules, sets the mode per risk tier from category risk, seller trust and listing score, with the synchronous gate and asynchronous re-scoring (book vs. first rental), time budgets per tier with the GMs, re-moderation of material edits (Which? December 2024) and a truthful description of the mode (leboncoin, Paris court, 2015).

The answer lists the shared machinery (decision service and record, enforcement events and monitor, case tooling, evidence store, statement-of-reasons service, rule runtime and lifecycle, registry with local content, base models), hashed block lists only with DPO approval (purpose, two-year retention, DPIA) and no raw messages, the per-brand overlays, thresholds, reviewers and vertical detectors, and sampled prevalence of fraudulent listings by brand with trend next to time to action on fraud reports instead of removals.
